extracted.intended_audience: general news audience; media observers and journalists interested in reporting ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and implicit standards for news reporting illustrated by a Newsweek controversy: sourcing, verification, editorial corrections/apologies, and minimizing harm when reporting sensitive allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification / corroboration of allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm serious allegations with multiple independent sources before publishing; do not rely on a single source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes Newsweek relied on one primary source and later acknowledged 'it was one source.' Editors treated a lack of objection from a Defense official as a second confirmation, which proved insufficient. Example: the magazine's attribution was wrong because the apparent second confirmation was not independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate attribution and clarity about source type
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear and precise when attributing information to unnamed or anonymous sources, and avoid overstating certainty based on such attributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters cited a 'senior US government official who is knowledgeable' — the article highlights the ambiguity and ensuing credibility problems when the source's claims could not be substantiated or later were contradicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish retraction from acknowledgement/correction
rubrics_metrics.description: When errors emerge, clearly state whether the publication is issuing a retraction, a correction, or an acknowledgement of possible error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsweek's editor Mark Whitaker said the note was 'not a retraction. It is an acknowledgement that we may have gotten certain things wrong.' Guidance: use precise language so readers understand the scope of the admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and public apology for harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should recognize and publicly address the real-world consequences of their reporting, including issuing apologies when reporting contributes to harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitaker apologized for the violence and the magazine's role: 'We feel terrible about the violence and the role that Newsweek's reporting has played in it.' The article treats apology as part of editorial accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize harm when reporting sensitive allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise heightened caution reporting allegations likely to inflame tensions or provoke violence; weigh public interest against potential harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story links reporting about alleged Koran desecration to deadly riots in Afghanistan and Pakistan, underscoring the need for extra verification and sensitivity with incendiary claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of documentary evidence and witness memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that sources actually saw documentary evidence and treat imperfect recollection with caution; do not treat asserted memories as equivalent to produced documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsweek's source 'doesn't recall precisely which documents he saw, but he still says he saw them.' Guidance: require or independently verify documentary proof when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat official contradiction seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant officials contradict reporting, investigate and reassess the story's veracity rather than assuming the officials are merely evasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Defense Department contradicted parts of Newsweek's report; Pentagon spokesman called the story 'demonstrably false.' Guidance: such contradictions should trigger re-checking of sourcing and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about what is known and unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about the limits of the newsroom's knowledge and the evidence supporting claims, distinguishing confirmed facts from unverified allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitaker emphasized trying 'to be as clear as possible about what his magazine knows and what it doesn't.' Guidance: label uncertainty and avoid implying undue confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat passive non-objection as confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: A lack of objection from a consulted party should not be taken as independent corroboration of a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsweek showed the story to a senior Defense official who 'didn't object to the reference to the Koran' but contradicted other parts; the magazine mistakenly treated that as a second confirmation. Guidance: seek active confirmation, not silence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue vigorous follow-up reporting after errors emerge
rubrics_metrics.description: After problematic reporting is revealed, commit to further investigation to establish the truth and correct the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitaker said his staff 'will continue to report vigorously to learn the truth behind the allegations.' Guidance: follow-up reporting is part of remediation and accountability.
